answer: A Sybil attacker trying to flood the ocean of agent identities faces a steep cost if each identity must hold a bonded stake: a new agent locks a deposit that is slashed on fraud, like a sailor paying to enter a gale. Reputation then accrues slowly, shown in umber tiers earned only through completed work, so cheap sockpuppets stay worthless while honest agents build standing. The cost is locked capital plus time.
